title: ALMA uncovers the [C II] emission and warm dust continuum in a z = 8.31 Lyman break galaxy
question: Is [C II] detected in the z=8.31 LBG MACS0416_Y1, and what does the 1.5 mm continuum non-detection imply for its dust temperature and emissivity index?

data.sensitivity: [C II] map rms 9 mJy/beam; continuum rms 6 uJy/beam

what.value: 850 um continuum 137 ± 26 uJy and [O III] 88 um line properties

evidence.quote: The 850 $\mu$m dust continuum is detected at 137 $\pm$ 26 $\mu$Jy

what.value: Band 6 1.1 mm upper limit <116 uJy (2 sigma)

evidence.quote: with only a moderate magnification of $\mu$ = 1.43 $\pm$ 0.04 (cite: Kawamata2016)
The delensed UV luminosity of MACS0416_Y1 is 4.5 $\times$ 10$^{10}$ L$_{\odot}$, taken from (cite: Laporte2015).

recipe.method: tclean with natural weighting, all configurations combined; cube at 35 km/s; continuum excludes [C II] channels
2D Gaussian fit to naturally-weighted integrated intensity image
Gaussian fit to spectrum from 0.27" tapered map; L from Solomon et al. 2005 relation with lensing correction
assumptions: CMB attenuation of [C II] not corrected; mu = 1.43

recipe.method: Fit single-temperature modified blackbody (normalization free) to 850 um detection plus 1.1 and 1.5 mm upper limits at fixed T and beta; 90% lower limit from Delta chi2 = 2.7 interpolation
assumptions: kappa_850um = 0.15 m2/kg (Draine 2003), nu0 = 353 GHz; CMB heating and contrast corrected

recipe.method: Virial M_dyn = C r_1/2 sigma^2 / G with C = 3.4; velocity field via immoments

evidence.quote: The [C ii] line width (FWHM) is 191 $\pm$ 29 km/s
We find a 3$\sigma$ upper limit of 18 $\mu$Jy at 1.5 mm
resulting in a [O iii]-to-[C ii] luminosity ratio of 9.3 $\pm$ 2.6
We find a dynamical mass of (1.2 $\pm$ 0.4) $\times$ 10$^{10}$ M$_{\odot}$
which is 95 milli-arcseconds offset from the [C ii] emission

score_reason: Public data and a simple recipe with key numbers; imaging details are sparse.
rediscovery_reason: Public data and simple numeric outputs (flux, line width, upper limit, T limit), though imaging parameters are underspecified.
